record.paper_title: Open problems in nuclear structure near drip lines
record.original_question: How should the Coulomb dissociation of two-neutron-halo nuclei be described when the emitted neutrons are correlated? Unlike one-neutron halo systems, where low-energy electric-dipole strength can often be interpreted as a single-particle transition from a weakly bound orbital to low-energy continuum orbitals, the open problem is to determine the role and form of two-neutron correlations in the dissociation process for halo nuclei with two loosely bound neutrons.

evidence.quote: In nuclei containing two or more loosely bound nucleons, however, the situation is not that simple as the correlation among these nucleons comes into the game. It has been discussed for a long time, but the correlation in the Coulomb dissociation process is still an open issue for two-neutron-halo nuclei [11, 12, 25].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-neutron halo nucleus, modeled as a tightly bound core plus two weakly bound valence neutrons whose separation energy is small compared to typical nuclear scales. When such a projectile passes a high-Z target at high beam energy, the time-dependent Coulomb field of the target can dissociate the projectile, ejecting the two halo neutrons into the continuum. For one-neutron halo nuclei, the low-energy electric-dipole (E1) strength distribution measured in Coulomb dissociation is well described as a single-particle transition of the loosely bound valence neutron from its bound orbital to low-energy continuum orbitals of the core+neutron system. For two-neutron halo nuclei, the two valence neutrons are dynamically correlated (through the neutron-neutron interaction and through Pauli/configuration mixing in the core+n+n system), and these correlations are expected to influence the breakup observables (E1 strength function, neutron-neutron and core-2n relative-energy spectra, opening-angle and momentum distributions of the fragments).

Develop a quantitative theoretical description of the Coulomb dissociation of a two-neutron halo nucleus that:
(i) incorporates the neutron-neutron correlation in the bound initial state and in the three-body continuum final state,
(ii) treats the electromagnetic excitation by the target field beyond the leading single-particle picture (including, where relevant, higher-order/continuum-continuum couplings and final-state interactions among the core and the two neutrons),
(iii) yields predictions for the low-energy E1 strength distribution, the core-2n and n-n invariant-mass spectra, and the angular correlations between the two emitted neutrons,
and determine, within this framework, the role and observable signatures of the two-neutron correlation (in particular, whether and to what extent a "dineutron"-like spatial correlation in the halo wave function is required to reproduce the measured Coulomb dissociation observables of two-neutron halo nuclei).
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature continues to investigate two-neutron correlations in Coulomb dissociation of halo nuclei (e.g., 11Li, 6He), with reviews on soft E1 excitation as a probe of n-n correlations and ongoing studies of dineutron correlations and continuum-continuum couplings. No consensus, fully predictive three-body theory is established; the role and quantitative form of two-neutron correlations in the dissociation process remains an active research question.

status_evidence.title: Coulomb Breakup and Soft E1 Excitation of Neutron Halo Nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Soft E1 excitation can be a probe of the neutron-neutron correlation of halo neutrons in two-neutron halo nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: The two-neutron correlation in Coulomb breakup is still actively studied as a probe rather than a settled description.

status_evidence.title: Renormalizing Two-Neutron Halo Nuclei Without Neutron-Core Interaction
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on the theoretical treatment of two-neutron halo nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical formulations of two-neutron halos continue to be developed, indicating the problem is not closed.

status_evidence.title: Coupling-in-the-continuum effects in Coulomb dissociation of halo nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Higher-order continuum couplings significantly affect partial-wave components beyond first-order approximation.
status_evidence.claim: Beyond-leading-order dynamics in Coulomb dissociation of halo nuclei remain an open theoretical issue.
